title: Quasi-affine parameter scheme for forms of a finite diagonalizable subgroup
statement: Let $A$ be any commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $M$ be a finite abelian group and let $H=D_A(M)\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $S$-scheme $W$, let $\mathcal P_H(W)$ be the set of closed subgroup schemes $K\hookrightarrow G_W=G\times_SW$ [def-pc-fibre-product] such that there exists an fppf covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] and isomorphisms of group schemes $K\times_WW_i\simeq H\times_SW_i$. This condition is on the abstract groups, not on their embeddings into $G_{W_i}$. Pullback makes $\mathcal P_H$ a contravariant functor. There is an $S$-scheme $Y_H$, with $Y_H\to S$ quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism] and of finite presentation, together with bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_S(W,Y_H)\simeq\mathcal P_H(W)$$ natural for every $S$-scheme $W$. This includes the trivial group $M=0$, the empty base, and characteristics dividing the order of $M$; no reducedness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4 and proof, printed pp.69-70. The functor is written using fppf forms of H; the source equivalently uses multiplicative-type subgroups geometrically isomorphic to H. The proof constructs it from the open embedding locus in Hom(H,G) modulo the finite constant automorphism group; no assertion about the conjugacy orbit or a homogeneous quotient is included here. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme structural assertion.

proof.text: The coordinate algebra $A[M]$ is free of rank $r=|M|\geq1$ over $A$. It has a finite algebra presentation, with generators $e_m$ and relations $e_0=1$, $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$; these relations reduce every monomial to one basis vector. Thus $H\to S$ is finite locally free. Apply the finite-flat-source group Hom theorem to $H,G$ to obtain an affine finitely presented scheme $B$ representing group homomorphisms $H_W\to G_W$. The universal point gives a homomorphism $u:H_B\to G_B$.

Apply the closed-embedding-locus theorem to $u$ over $B$. It gives a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq B$ representing closed subgroup embeddings $H_W\hookrightarrow G_W$. An open immersion is etale, hence locally of finite presentation; composition with $B\to S$ is locally of finite presentation. Moreover $V$ is a quasi-compact open in the affine scheme $B$, so it is quasi-affine and separated, and $V\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. It follows that $V\to S$ is of finite presentation. All of this holds over the original ring $A$.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, open embedding locus; arbitrary-ring refinement recorded in the locus node.

proof.text: Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Aut}(M)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Character duality identifies $\operatorname{Aut}_{W\text{-gp}}(H_W)$ with the locally constant maps $|W|\to\Gamma$: apply its local description on nonempty affine opens, and glue the unique homomorphisms. The empty affine case has one section on either side. Since $M$ is finite, $\Gamma$ is finite, so this automorphism functor is the constant group scheme $\Gamma_S$. It acts on $B$ by precomposition and preserves $V$. On every scheme test, $j\circ\gamma=j$ for an embedding $j$ implies $\gamma=1$, by cancellation of the monomorphism $j$. Hence the action on $V$ is free.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, constant automorphism group and its free action.

proof.text: Every point orbit in $V$ is finite and is contained in an affine open of $V$. Indeed write $B=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $B\setminus V=V(I)$. If the nonempty orbit corresponds to primes $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_n$, then $I\not\subset\mathfrak p_i$. Prime avoidance gives $a\in I\setminus\bigcup_i\mathfrak p_i$, and the affine principal open $D(a)$ contains the orbit and lies in $V$. Also $V$ is absolutely separated, as an open of the affine $B$. The admissible free finite-group quotient theorem therefore gives a separated scheme $Q$, a finite etale surjection $q:V\to Q$, and $V\times_QV\simeq\Gamma_S\times_SV$. As fppf covers are fpqc, $S$ is an fppf sheaf by representable descent, so the universal property descends the invariant map $V\to S$ to $Q\to S$. The represented fppf orbit quotient is also the orbit quotient on $S$-scheme tests.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, quotient construction; Stacks Tags 07S6 and 0BBM replace the source quotient citation.

proof.text: The torsor $q$ has constant degree $|\Gamma|\geq1$: after pulling back by $q$ it is the projection from the disjoint union of $|\Gamma|$ copies of $V$; equivalently its finite etale geometric fibres have exactly $|\Gamma|$ points, by freeness and the orbit description. Being finite and etale, hence flat and locally of finite presentation, it is finite locally free of this degree, and quasi-affine reflection gives that $Q\to S$ is quasi-affine. Local finite presentation of $V\to S$ descends along the flat locally finitely presented surjection $q$. Finally, $Q$ is quasi-compact since $V$ is, and quasi-separated since it is separated. As $S$ is affine these imply quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $Q\to S$. Consequently $Q\to S$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, quasi-affineness and finite presentation; Stacks 0BD1, 0BD2 for quasi-affineness.

proof.text: The universal embedding over $V$ gives a closed subgroup $K_V\subseteq G_V$, finite locally free of degree $r$. On $V\times_QV\simeq\Gamma_S\times_SV$ the two pullbacks are equal as closed subschemes, since precomposition changes the embedding but not its image. The finite etale surjection $q$ is fppf, hence fpqc. Effective descent of finite locally free closed subschemes yields a unique $K_Q\subseteq G_Q$ with pullback $K_V$ and degree $r$. Its group structure descends as well: on each test scheme, the identity, products and inverses of sections factor through $K_Q$ after the pulled-back fpqc cover; the local lifts into $K_Q$ agree by its monomorphism into $G_Q$ and glue by representable descent. This proves the subgroup diagrams, which can likewise be checked after that cover. Since $q^*K_Q\simeq H_V$, every base change of $K_Q$ is an fppf form of $H$.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, quotient identifies with the subgroup functor; Stacks 03I0 for embedded descent.

proof.text: Conversely let $K\subseteq G_W$ be an fppf form of $H_W$. Choose its stated trivializations over $W_i\to W$. Their composites with $K_{W_i}\hookrightarrow G_{W_i}$ give points $v_i:W_i\to V$. On overlaps two embeddings with the same closed image differ by a unique automorphism of $H$, hence by a section of $\Gamma$ from character duality. Thus $qv_i=qv_j$ on overlaps. Fppf covers are fpqc, so representable descent glues these maps to a unique $h:W\to Q$. The pullback $h^*K_Q$ is $K$: check on the covering $W_i\times_QV\to W_i$ and use uniqueness of embedded descent. Starting with $h$ recovers $h$, because this construction agrees with it on the fppf cover $W\times_QV\to W$. Therefore the constructions are mutually inverse. Each construction uses pullback of embeddings, maps and closed subschemes, so the bijection commutes with every $W'\to W$. Take $Y_H=Q$.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.4, p.70, injectivity and local surjectivity; fppf-forms formulation.

proof.text: If $A=0$, all schemes over $S$ are empty and the construction gives the unique represented functor on that base. If $M=0$, $H$ is the trivial group; there is one embedding into any $G_W$, namely the identity section, and any form of the trivial group is trivial. Thus $B=V=Q=S$. In characteristics dividing $|M|$, $A[M]$ is still finite free and the automorphism scheme is still constant finite etale; no step requires $H$ to be reduced or its order to be invertible. These cases are therefore included.

source.place: Edge-case check of the same construction.
